key_insight: LLM-to-Flow Distillation teaches scientific generators to pursue natural-language discovery goals using an adaptive, frozen LLM teacher rather than an explicit proxy reward.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support anticancer peptide discovery, but the abstract does not establish experimental efficacy, safety, or clinical benefit.
method: The LLM builds intermediate goals tailored to the generator’s current capabilities.
The LLM judges generated candidates to create preference signals.
Direct preference optimization (DPO) iteratively aligns the generator with the discovery goal.
evidence_signal: Experiments on therapeutic peptides and small-molecule structure design demonstrate goal-directed generative control, though the abstract reports no quantitative results or experimental validation.
watch_item: LLM-derived preferences may not reflect biological activity, so generated candidates require independent experimental validation.
paper_title: LLM-to-Flow Distillation: Teaching Natural Language Goals to Scientific Generators
